question.text: 'Lotus Growth Partners AIF' is drafting side letters that give large investors participation rights in the IC. The chapter warns that the investment manager has a fiduciary duty towards ALL investors. The recommended mechanism to avoid breach of fiduciary duty when granting differential rights is:

answer.text: Get written consent of every other investor before granting side letter rights
Create a separate class of units with differential rights, issued to large investors
Route side letter rights through the trustee rather than the manager
Limit differential rights to a 30-day trial period

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.4.1, to avoid breach of fiduciary duty owed to all investors, most investment managers create a separate class of units with differential rights issued to large investors. This makes the differential treatment a function of the unit class (transparent to all), rather than a bilateral side deal. The Trap: Individual consent from every LP is impractical. Trustee routing does not cure fiduciary breach. A time-limit mechanism doesn't solve the parity issue.
